name: dying-music-box
style: Instrumental, 17 seconds, music box horror miniature. 3am in an empty corner shop under buzzing strip lights, and a tune starts from nowhere: a tiny wind-up music box, celesta shadowing it note for note, plucking a five-note minor lullaby in a lopsided limping meter, repeating like a child humming. Close and dry, the comb's teeth and the clockwork ticking right in your ear, a cold fluorescent hum underneath. The spring is running out: each pass a little slower, the pitch sagging flat, notes stretching apart. Three bright metallic plinks snap out of the middle like a light flickering, then the tune drags to almost nothing and one deep struck bell lands, and stops dead, only the hum left ringing for a breath.

name: distorted-industrial-theme
style: Industrial horror instrumental, E minor, 90 BPM half-time. Detuned upright piano slammed through tape saturation and a heavy bitcrusher, playing a fast nervous minor-key ostinato in the high octaves, high-pass filtered and thin at first over a sidechained sub drone that pumps. Downtuned baritone electric guitar on one low E, palm-muted, hits three separate slams two seconds apart, each slam doubled by an anvil strike and a struck steel sheet in a gated room. After the third slam the filter rips open: guitar chugs eighths on the low E, crushed piano screams on top, metal clanks tighten. Ends on one enormous slam of everything at once, then a hard cut to dead silence, no tail. Tight, dry, clipped transients, cold, close-miked. No vocals, instrumental only.

name: horror-trailer-strings
style: Instrumental 17-second horror film teaser cue for chamber string orchestra, composer's brief. Opens in near silence: a low cello drone on a single open note, dry col legno tapping in the violas ticking like a slow clock, faint distant growls and clicks under the floor. Violins enter sul ponticello tremolo, thin and glassy near the bridge, creeping upward in a slow chromatic glissando; artificial harmonics shimmer on top like cold fluorescent light. Around 6, 8 and 9 seconds: three vicious full-section string stabs, sforzando, each sharper than the last, with dead air between. After the third stab a deep braam-like low brass swell rises and fills the room. At 15 seconds one huge final orchestral hit, then abrupt trailer silence, and a single high violin harmonic left hanging, very quiet, until it fades. Close mic, dark, minor, atonal clusters, cinematic, dry room with a long cold tail.

name: fluorescent-sound-design
style: instrumental, foley soundscape rather than a song, no groove, no tune. Recorded close in a cramped night shop with tiled floor: the 100 Hz mains buzz of an ageing strip light, gritty and steady, tuned to sit just under a low G and swelling into a dark minor drone; a chiller cabinet compressor shuddering awake and ticking; a hinge groaning as a glass door eases open; three sour notes from a neglected, detuned pub upright, far apart, every note answered by a sharp arcing crackle and the strip light stuttering; distant hollow room tone from a back store. Last moments: a heavy subsonic thud, one bright glassy tink from the tube, then a relay click and the buzz is gone, total silence.
